The micropores of the carbon are ∼0.5 nm in size.

The solvent molecule of the electrolyte is ∼0.7 nm in diameter.

The sodium ion is ∼0.2 nm in diameter.

Because the micropores are smaller than the solvent molecule, the sodium ion must desolvate at the surface of the microporous host and transport independently to the sulfur, forming a quasi-solid-state reaction at the cathode.
